clue.text: Spar with a lump outside for medal

indicators.note: the lump is placed outside the other pieces, so it wraps around them

parts.note: a burr is a rough lump or knot, as on a tree trunk
a mast is a spar, a pole carrying a ship's sails

explanation.surface: Sparring partners wrestling while one carries a bump, all for a medal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spar' looks like a verb for boxing but is the ship's pole. Vera Lynn toured Burma to entertain the troops.
explanation.definitionFit: The Burma Star is a British campaign medal awarded for service in Burma in the Second World War.

definitions.meaning: to dip the head or body in greeting
the forward end of a ship
an archer's weapon that shoots arrows

explanation.surface: Lower the tip of a weapon, as in a salute.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition: three different senses of one three-letter word, with 'of' as the link.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word means a bending of the head, the forward part of a vessel, and the archer's arrow-shooting tool.

indicators.note: taking the top off the word removes its first letter

parts.note: to braise is to stew food slowly in a covered pot

explanation.surface: A cook lifts the lid from a pot of stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top off' removes B, the first letter of BRAISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to lift something is to raise it.

indicators.note: the word 'to' gives only its starting letter here
rejecting the word turns it back on itself, so it is read from the end

parts.note: a liar tells stories that are untrue

explanation.surface: A storyteller starting to turn away a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starting' takes T from 'to'; 'reject' turns LIAR into RAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as verbs: to dog someone is to follow or track them closely.

indicators.note: a stew is a muddle or jumble, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A casserole prepared ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stew' rearranges MADE EARLY. The whole clue also defines: a convenience dish prepared in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: A supermarket dish cooked ahead of time and simply reheated, such as a stew, fits the whole clue's description.

clue.text: Know-alls are told lie during kisses

indicators.note: these pieces go during, that is inside, the other word

parts.note: smacks are loud kisses

indicators.note: told means spoken, so the word 'are' is taken by how it is said

parts.note: said out loud, this word sounds like the letter R
a tale is a lie or fib

explanation.surface: Smug people tell fibs while kissing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'told' means the word 'are' counts only by its sound, the letter R; 'during' puts that and the fib inside the kisses.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: know-alls are conceited people who claim to know everything, the same as cocky clever-clogs.

indicators.note: cooking up suggests concocting, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man from the Basque country is preparing a pufferfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' rearranges A BASQUES.
explanation.definitionFit: Example of a name: the sea squab is a puffer or blowfish of the Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Protection for car wing-like in 50% of automatics

indicators.note: the wing-like word sits in the half-word
half of the ten-letter word, its first five letters

parts.note: alar is an adjective meaning of or like a wing

explanation.surface: Something about cars with wings, half of them automatics.
explanation.walkthrough: '50% of' keeps the first five of the ten letters; 'in' puts the wing word inside them. 'wing-like' suggests car bodywork but is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle's anti-theft siren system guards it against thieves, a form of protection.

indicators.note: the chair holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a throne is a ceremonial chair

indicators.note: regular letters are every other one, here the second, fourth, sixth and eighth

explanation.surface: The chair of Trinity College keeps redesigning things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regular' takes the even letters of 'redesigns'; 'holding' puts them inside the seat. The 's after Trinity is a link, 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christian doctrine of God as Father, Son and Spirit describes a single Godhead of three persons.

clue.text: One of a group from 19, 12 that'll be beneath Sialia

definitions.text: One of a group from 19, 12 that'll be beneath Sialia

parts.words: One of a group from 19, 12 that'll be beneath Sialia
parts.note: Sialia is the scientific genus of bluebirds; Vera Lynn, the 19/12, sang that bluebirds would fly over these chalk faces of Dover

explanation.surface: A puzzling reference to something lying under a genus of birds.
explanation.walkthrough: Vera Lynn's wartime song promised bluebirds over the chalk coast of Dover; this is one of those cliffs, beneath the birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic: the chalk faces at Dover are the landmark the bluebirds of the song fly over.

indicators.note: to change the letters is to rearrange them

explanation.surface: A chemistry instruction: alter a reagent without effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges A REACTANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom from riding: going at a gentle gallop means doing something comfortably without strain.

parts.note: Luscinia is the nightingale genus; Vera Lynn sang 'A Nightingale Sang in' this London square

explanation.surface: A question about where a singer's songbird made music.
explanation.walkthrough: Luscinia is the Latin genus of the nightingale, and 'made notes' means sang, pointing to the famous song title.
explanation.definitionFit: The London square in Mayfair is the setting named in the nightingale song Vera Lynn recorded.

definitions.meaning: a spring or shaft from which water is drawn
sound as in healthy, in good condition

explanation.surface: Where a noise comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: One word means a spring of water and also means healthy, the sense of sound in 'safe and sound'.

clue.text: Drink up like king and live with queen

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: regal means kingly, like a king
to be is to live or exist
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Drink up like a king and then live with the queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns REGAL into LAGER in this down clue; 'Drink up' looks like one phrase but 'Drink' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a pale lager is a type of drink served in pubs.

clue.text: Just one proceeds to attend reunion

parts.note: meet is an old word for fitting or just
A means one, as in a single thing
proceeds are takings or gain

explanation.surface: Only one of the profits goes to the reunion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like 'only' but means fitting, an archaic sense. Vera Lynn's best-known song is 'We'll Meet Again'.
explanation.definitionFit: To come together once more after separation is to go to a gathering of old friends.

clue.text: A number imprisoned by post-Imperial king in cruel deceit

indicators.note: imprisoned by means placed inside the other word

parts.note: metric measures replaced the old Imperial units of weight and length in Britain
taken as written
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A prisoner held by a king after the end of empire, in a nasty trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imprisoned by' puts AN inside METRIC; 'post-Imperial' looks like history but refers to Imperial measures.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a nasty, unkind trick is a cruel deception.

clue.text: Simpson turns up in sound border town

indicators.note: the turned name sits in the other word

parts.note: sound in mind means sane

indicators.note: in a down clue, turns up means the name is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: Bart Simpson, from the TV cartoon

explanation.surface: A Simpson arrives at a quiet frontier settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reads the cartoon boy's name from the bottom in this down clue; 'in' puts it inside the word for sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Strabane is a town in Northern Ireland on the border with the Republic of Ireland.

clue.text: Big and tall he's flailing around last in pool

indicators.note: flailing around suggests wild disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A large tall man thrashing about in a swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flailing around' rearranges BIG and TALL HE; 'pool' is the cue game, not the swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: In the game of pool, the black ball numbered eight is the one potted last to win.

indicators.note: the fish's name is turned back to front

parts.note: Nemo is the clownfish in the film Finding Nemo

explanation.surface: A sign that a cartoon clownfish has returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is back' turns NEMO around.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a portent or sign of things to come.

clue.text: Newton Dyne could be love song performer

parts.note: the newton and the dyne are units of force, so they could be forces
a sweetheart is a love, a beloved

explanation.surface: A man called Newton Dyne might sing love songs.
explanation.walkthrough: Newton Dyne looks like a person's name but is two units of force.
explanation.definitionFit: The wartime nickname of the singer Vera Lynn, who entertained British troops.

clue.text: Extreme right turn more difficult when reported by celebrity panel

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: harder means more difficult
a star is a celebrity
a board is a panel, of wood or of people

explanation.surface: A tougher U-turn announced by a panel of famous judges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when reported' gives HARDA from how 'harder' is said. 'right' is the nautical side, starboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A helm order meaning to steer as far as possible to the right, the starboard side of a ship.

indicators.note: terrible implies a wrecked state, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who suffered Goneril's fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges ANGER. The 's after Goneril is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's King Lear, Goneril poisons her sister, Lear's second daughter.

indicators.note: taking the start off the word removes its first letter

parts.note: brainy means bright or clever

explanation.surface: A weather forecast: sunny at first, then showers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start off' drops B from BRAINY; 'bright' looks like weather but means clever.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather with showers is wet weather, a day of rain.

parts.note: ave is a Latin greeting, hail or welcome
raging means wild or furious

explanation.surface: An invitation to a wild night out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evening out' looks like a night on the town but means levelling out.
explanation.definitionFit: Levelling things to a mean value is smoothing out differences.

explanation.surface: A trendy kind of nightclub.
explanation.definitionFit: One word means to waft air to chill, and also describes a club of admirers of a star.

indicators.note: done badly, the letters come out in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A gardener who pruned the trees poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges TREES; 'Clipped' looks like pruning but means curt.
explanation.definitionFit: Clipped speech is brief and curt, the same as brusque.

clue.text: Film Gandhi missing the latest news of Norfolk town

indicators.note: missing means that letter is left out of the actor's name

parts.note: Ben Kingsley played Gandhi in the 1982 film

indicators.note: the latest letter of 'the' is its final one

parts.note: news taken as plural of N for new, giving two Ns

explanation.surface: The film Gandhi lacks the latest news from a Norfolk town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the latest' gives E, which 'missing' drops from KINGSLEY. NN for 'news' treats it as two abbreviated 'new's. King's Lynn is a market town in Norfolk, eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: King's Lynn is a port and market town in the English county of Norfolk.
